identity.description: Threads, Meta's text-based social network (threads.com / threads.net). The Threads API is Meta's developer API for publishing and reading Threads content, replies, mentions, insights and profiles. Matches the requested product.
identity.identity_notes: Meta's developer docs describe the Threads API as a way to 'create and publish posts, retrieve media and profiles, moderate replies, and access insights.' Hostnames graph.threads.com / threads.com confirm it is the Threads social product.

auth.oauth_flows: Authorization-code flow: user approves in an Authorization Window at https://threads.com/oauth/authorize, Threads redirects with a code, and the app exchanges it via POST https://graph.threads.com/oauth/access_token. Short-lived token valid 1 hour, exchangeable for a long-lived token valid 60 days. App access tokens (client credentials from app ID and secret) are used for some endpoints such as oEmbed.
auth.token_refresh: Short-lived tokens can be exchanged for long-lived tokens (60 days). Refresh of long-lived tokens is not documented in the fetched pages.
auth.scopes_notes: scope values listed: threads_basic (required), threads_content_publish, threads_read_replies, threads_manage_replies, threads_manage_insights. Page does not explain what each scope permits. Permission grants by app users with public profiles are valid for 90 days.

access.production_restrictions: Each permission must pass App Review and the app must be published before app users without a role on the app can use it. Test users must be invited and accept the invitation to the Threads profile. Webhooks Live notifications require Live mode (non-tech providers) or advanced access (tech providers) and a verified business. Public server required for media URLs. Business verification is linked but its exact requirement is not stated.

resources: Media retrieval by ID or keyword
User profile, posts, replies, mentions, ghost posts, publishing limit
read_ops: Retrieve media by ID or keyword
Retrieve user profile, posts, replies, mentions, ghost posts, publishing limit
Look up public profiles and posts

write_ops: Upload and publish media (single and carousel posts)
api.rate_limits: Not documented in the fetched pages.
api.limitations: Write surface centers on publishing and reply moderation; no DM, no follower management documented. Endpoint HTTP methods and paths were not shown on the reference index page. Rate limits not found.

open_questions: Rate limits for the Threads API are not found in the fetched pages; need the rate-limit/ Graph API docs.
Whether long-lived tokens can be refreshed, and the refresh endpoint, were not confirmed.
Whether Development-mode apps with Threads Testers role can call all endpoints without App Review was not explicitly stated.
Business verification requirement for standard vs advanced access is unclear; the page only links it.
Endpoint HTTP methods and exact paths (e.g., /{threads-user-id}/threads, /threads_publish) were not visible in fetched pages.
No official Meta-published MCP server was found; a check of github.com/facebook or github.com/facebookarchive for threads MCP was not done.
A developer forum post reported an 'insufficient access tier' error on a Threads oEmbed permission test during App Review; unresolved and anecdotal.
Official Postman workspace for the Threads API was referenced by a community listing but not verified on Meta's site.
Composio hosts a Threads toolkit (composio.dev/toolkits/threads); that is a commercial hosted connector, not a vendor MCP server.

rationale: Self-serve test credentials (free self serve) and a documented REST interface.
Production/public use requires vendor app review.
